history.period: 12th century (medieval); exact dates vary across sources and are unverified
history.summary: The Siddheshwar and Ratneshwar Temple at Hake Nagar, about 2 km from Latur city, is a Shiva temple built in Western Indian stone architecture. The gabhara (sanctum) — a 25x15 ft original construction — carries a shikhar about 9.14 m above terrace level; inside it a copper facial plaque of Lord Siddheshwar sits on a pedestal with a Shiva linga established in a small kund below. A later cement-concrete sabhamandap with 18 large pillars (capacity ~3,000, open on the sides) and a temple kund complete the precinct. Local tradition says King Tamradwaj built it as a mark of respect to Siddharameshwar of Solapur, the 12th-century Lingayat/Veerashaiva saint-poet, and the temple reflects the 12th-century Veerashaiva devotional milieu. An annual fair is held here on Mahashivratri. CSV name 'Shri Siddheshwar Temple' maps cleanly to this documented temple (listed variously as Siddheshwar Temple / Siddheshwar Ratneshwar Mandir).

town_description: Latur is a major city in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, known as an educational and trading hub with the distinctive circular Ganjgolai market at its centre. It lies about 2-3 hours south of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and is the administrative seat of Latur district.
